rationale: 2 critical + 3 major findings: kind:'input' controls never mask secret values (credential/API-key text is shown and permanently echoed in cleartext, CR-004) and profileName's open-row heading is hardcoded rather than message-derived per the spec's own rule (CR-003); commit-format violates git-workflow.md on 9 of 10 commit subjects (CR-001), the driver's model-branch mirror of the new list-echo fix has no dedicated regression test (CR-002), and setup-view.js's start() lacks a re-entrancy guard (CR-005, dev-console-only path). The disclosed ratified exception touching ui/setup-driver.js (3ff82f8) was reviewed at full rigor and found correct, minimal, and non-regressive against its own invariants; per the task's directive the file-touch itself is not a finding, so its business_review row is 'na' rather than 'fail'. 10 lens-reported candidates were checked against the real CLI/source and dismissed as unreachable or already-guarded; 0 findings deferred.

findings.title: Commit subjects skip the conventional type prefix
findings.problem: 9 of 10 'EPMCDME-14513: ...' commit subjects in this range use the ticket id as the leading token instead of a type in feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor, e.g. 'EPMCDME-14513: wire setup-view dev hook (task 8)'.
findings.impact: git-workflow.md's commit-format standard is treated as always-blocking by this gate, so the range as committed fails the standards audit outright.
findings.recommendation: Prefix each commit subject with the correct conventional type (feat:/fix:/test:/refactor:/chore:) and move the ticket id into the body, matching git-workflow.md's own examples.

findings.title: Model-branch answeredOnce fix has no regression test
findings.problem: The list-answered-echo fix mirrors the provider-list fix in the same diff by adding answeredOnce.add(prompt.id) for the 'model' branch (line 463), but every existing model-related test (the CR-002 pagination test and the REAL-terminal pagination test) exits the fake PTY from inside onPrompt before any answer write or echo chunk is fed back, so neither reaches this line's post-answer path.
findings.impact: If this line is reverted or the model branch's answeredOnce marking regresses, the model prompt's answered echo would be re-dispatched to onPrompt a second time and the caller would answer it again -- the same class of bug the new provider-echo test exists to catch -- and no test in setup-driver.test.mjs would fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a model-answered-echo fixture (analogous to provider-answered-then-next-open.json) and a test asserting onPrompt is called exactly once for id:'model' with no second arrow-key/answer write.

findings.title: profileName heading is hardcoded, not message-derived
findings.problem: PROMPT_COPY.profileName.heading is the fixed string 'Profile name', and headingFor() always returns it for this prompt, overriding rowTitleFor()'s message-derived title. The spec states this row's title and default value are derived per the same general rule as codemieUrl/credential, with the wireframe's static caption describing only the mockup.
findings.impact: The open-row heading always shows the generic 'Profile name' instead of the CLI's actual question text ('Enter a name for this profile'), a real -- if narrow -- deviation from an explicit spec requirement; no test in the diff exercises the open-row title for a profileName prompt to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Drop the heading override in PROMPT_COPY.profileName (keep collapsedLabel) so headingFor() falls back to rowTitleFor()'s message-derived title, matching codemieUrl/credential; add a test asserting the open-row title for id:'profileName'.

findings.title: Secret input is never masked and is echoed in cleartext
findings.problem: renderInputControl() always creates input.type='text' regardless of prompt id or message, and renderControl()'s submit() sets the collapsed row's permanent subtitle to the raw entered value via stepsUi.setSubtitle(rowId, text). This includes the 'credential' catch-all id, which setup-driver.js's own comments confirm carries secrets the CLI marks hidden (e.g. 'AWS Secret Access Key: [hidden]').
findings.impact: An API key or cloud secret typed into guided setup is shown in clear text on screen while typing and remains visible in clear text in the completed row afterward, exposing it to shoulder-surfing, screen recording, or screenshots.
findings.recommendation: Give input-kind prompts whose id/message signals a secret (id 'credential', or a message containing '[hidden]'/'[input is hidden]') a masked input.type='password' control, and store/display a redacted placeholder (e.g. 'Set') as the row's subtitle instead of the raw value.

findings.title: start() has no re-entrancy guard
findings.problem: start() is exposed via the dev-only window.__codemie.startGuidedSetup hook with no guard preventing a second invocation on the same view instance while a prior run has not settled; occurrenceCounts/baseMessageByPromptId/activeRowId/container state and the DOM are all reset/cleared unconditionally at the top of start().
findings.impact: A second concurrent start() call (reachable only via the devtools console hook, not a production UI path) clears the container and resets state out from under the first run's still-pending onPrompt/handleResolve callbacks, corrupting both runs with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Add a simple running flag: throw or no-op if start() is called again before the previous call's promise has settled.
